components.name: Accordion
components.description: The Accordion component is a flexible UI primitive built with React and TypeScript. It allows users to expand and collapse content sections, making it ideal for FAQs, documentation, and content-heavy interfaces.

props.name: items
props.description: The accordion items to render, in order.

props.name: allowMultiple
props.description: When true, multiple items can stay open at once; when false (default), opening an item closes any other open item.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Indexes of items that start open.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root wrapper element.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root wrapper element.

props.name: itemClassName
props.description: Classes for each item's outer container.

props.name: itemStyle
props.description: Inline styles for each item's outer container.

props.name: headerClassName
props.description: Classes for each item's clickable header button.

props.name: headerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for each item's clickable header button — applied unconditionally, not only on hover.

props.name: titleClassName
props.description: Classes for the title text span inside the header.

props.name: titleStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the title text span inside the header.

props.name: iconClassName
props.description: Classes for the expand/collapse icon wrapper.

props.name: iconStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the expand/collapse icon wrapper.

props.name: contentWrapperClassName
props.description: Classes for the collapsible grid wrapper around the content.

props.name: contentWrapperStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the collapsible grid wrapper around the content.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Classes for the inner content container.

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the inner content container.

props.name: hoverClassName
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the header last, so they can override the built-in hover styling; note they apply at rest too, not only on hover.

props.name: hoverStyle
props.description: Extra inline styles merged onto the header; since inline styles can't express :hover, these apply unconditionally. Prefer hoverClassName.

props.name: borderColor
props.description: Declared for future theming but not currently applied anywhere in the render.

props.name: radius
props.description: Declared for future theming but not currently applied anywhere in the render.

props.name: shadow
props.description: Declared for future theming but not currently applied anywhere in the render.

props.name: duration
props.description: Duration in milliseconds of the expand/collapse grid-row transition.

props.name: iconOpen
props.description: Custom icon shown when an item is open; defaults to a ChevronUp.

props.name: iconClose
props.description: Custom icon shown when an item is closed; defaults to a ChevronDown.

props.name: renderItem
props.type: (params: { item: AccordionItem; index: number; open: boolean; toggle: () => void; }) => ReactNode
props.description: Fully custom renderer for each item, replacing the default header/content markup. Receives the item, its index, open state, and a toggle callback.

avoid: Hiding primary information inside Accordions

rules.title: Accordion
rules.content:
Use Accordion when information is optional or secondary.

Good:

* FAQs
* Advanced settings
* Documentation sections
* Additional details

Do not hide primary information inside Accordions.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

components.name: ActionSheet
components.description: A bottom sheet of contextual actions. It slides up from the bottom edge on phones and becomes a centered card on wider screens, traps focus while open, locks page scroll, respects safe-area insets and reduced motion, and supports destructive and disabled actions.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state; omit to let the sheet manage it internally.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state in uncontrolled mode.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called whenever the sheet should open or close, controlled or not.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading shown above the actions; also the dialog's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional supporting text below the title.

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions listed in the sheet.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Label for the dismiss button.

props.name: hideCancel
props.description: Hides the separate Cancel button.

props.name: closeOnOverlayClick
props.description: Close the sheet when the overlay is clicked.

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Close the sheet with the Escape key.

props.name: className
props.description: Styles the bottom panel.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the bottom panel.

props.name: overlayClassName
props.description: Styles the dimmed overlay behind the panel.

props.name: headerClassName
props.description: Styles the title + description block.

props.name: titleClassName
props.description: Styles the title heading.

props.name: descriptionClassName
props.description: Styles the description text.

props.name: actionsClassName
props.description: Styles the list wrapping the action buttons.

props.name: actionClassName
props.description: Applied to every action button.

props.name: cancelClassName
props.description: Styles the Cancel button.

useFor: Short lists of actions for one item on mobile
Mobile list of actions for one item
avoid: Desktop menus
Desktop menus (use Dropdown or ContextMenu)

rules.title: Drawer
rules.content:
Use Drawer for contextual content that should remain connected to the current page.

Good:

* Filters
* Detail views
* Editing
* Mobile navigation
* Secondary settings

Drawer is especially useful when the user should keep the underlying page context.

rules.title: Dropdown
rules.content:
Use Dropdown for actions or compact menus.

Good:

```text
More
 ├── Edit
 ├── Duplicate
 ├── Archive
 └── Delete
```

Do not use Dropdown when users need to compare multiple persistent options.

Use Select instead for form selection.

components.name: ActivityHeatmap
components.description: A calendar-aligned contribution grid for commits, deploys, logins or any daily metric. Every column is one week, every row is one weekday, and the intensity ramp is built from your theme tokens.

props.name: data
props.description: Daily activity records; dates may be ISO strings ("2024-03-05") or Date objects. Missing days count as 0.

props.name: weeks
props.description: Number of trailing weeks to display, ending at the latest date; defaults to the full data range.

props.name: endDate
props.description: Last day shown in the grid; defaults to the latest date in `data`.

props.name: colorScale
props.description: Semantic token family used for the intensity ramp.

props.name: size
props.description: Cell size preset.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Shows the "Less / More" legend under the grid.

props.name: showWeekdayLabels
props.description: Shows Mon / Wed / Fri labels beside the grid.

props.name: showMonthLabels
props.description: Shows month labels above the grid.

props.name: formatLabel
props.description: Builds the accessible label and tooltip for each day.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the whole heatmap.

props.name: onDayClick
props.type: (day: { date: string | Date; count: number }) => void
props.description: Called when a day cell is clicked; makes every cell a focusable button.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the heatmap root.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the heatmap root.

props.name: gridClassName
props.description: Styles the scrollable grid wrapper (labels + columns).

props.name: cellClassName
props.description: Styles every day cell.

props.name: labelClassName
props.description: Styles the month and weekday labels.

props.name: legendClassName
props.description: Styles the legend row.

useFor: Daily activity density over weeks (contributions, deploys, usage)
requirements: Keep KPI tiles numbers first; add a chart only where a trend or comparison helps.
Dashboard charts must use apexcharts + react-apexcharts with theme CSS variables, inside a Card with CardHeader and CardBody.

rules.title: Dashboard Charts
rules.content:
When you build a dashboard (analytics, admin, CRM, reports, any page that shows stats over time or comparisons), visualize the stats with ApexCharts using `apexcharts` + `react-apexcharts`. Do not use another chart library and do not fake charts with divs or static images.

Install:

```bash
npm install apexcharts react-apexcharts
```

Usage (Next.js: load the chart client-side only):

```jsx
"use client";
import dynamic from "next/dynamic";
const Chart = dynamic(() => import("react-apexcharts"), { ssr: false });

const css = (name) =>
  getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name).trim();

const options = {
  chart: { toolbar: { show: false }, fontFamily: "inherit", background: "transparent" },
  colors: [css("--primary"), css("--info"), css("--warning")],
  grid: { borderColor: css("--border"), strokeDashArray: 4 },
  xaxis: { categories, labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  yaxis: { labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  tooltip: { theme: isDark ? "dark" : "light" },
  dataLabels: { enabled: false },
  stroke: { curve: "smooth", width: 2 },
};

<Chart type="area" height={300} options={options} series={series} />
```

Rules:

* Chart colors come from the theme CSS variables (read with getComputedStyle), never hardcoded hex values. Re-read them when the theme switches between light and dark.
* Place each chart inside a Card with a CardHeader (title, short description, optional range selector) and the chart in CardBody.
* Pick the chart by the question: line/area for trends over time, bar for comparing categories, donut/radial only for a few parts of a whole (max 5 slices), sparkline inside stat tiles.
* Keep KPI stat tiles as numbers first; add a chart only where a trend or comparison helps.
* Hide the toolbar, disable data labels on dense series, keep the grid subtle, and set an explicit height so the layout does not jump while loading.
* Charts must be responsive: use `width="100%"` and stack chart cards to a single column on small screens.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.description: A confirmation dialog for decisions that need an explicit answer. It is announced as an alert dialog, focuses Cancel first, blocks Escape and overlay clicks by default, and supports a typed confirmation and async confirm actions with a loading state.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state; omit to let the dialog manage it internally.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state in uncontrolled mode.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called whenever the open state changes, controlled or not.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog heading, also used as the accessible name.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy rendered under the heading.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Label of the primary action button.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Label of the button that dismisses the dialog.

props.name: tone
props.description: Visual treatment of the primary action.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon; defaults to a warning icon for the destructive tone. Pass `null` to hide it.

props.name: requireText
props.description: When set, the confirm button stays disabled until this exact text is typed.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called when the primary action is confirmed. If it returns a promise, the confirm button shows a spinner and the dialog closes once it resolves (and stays open if it rejects).

rules.title: Modal
rules.content:
Use Modal for focused decisions or short tasks.

Good:

* Confirm deletion
* Create item
* Edit item
* Important settings
* Focused forms

Do not use Modal for:

* Long documentation
* Large dashboards
* Complex workflows
* Information that deserves its own page

If the content requires significant scrolling, consider a page or Drawer instead.

Modal overflow, compulsory:

* A Modal must never grow taller than the viewport. Cap the modal body height (for example `max-h-[70vh]` or `max-h-[calc(100vh-8rem)]`) and give the body `overflow-y-auto`.
* Only the body scrolls. Keep the header (title, close button) and footer (actions) fixed and always visible.
* Never let content be clipped or push the action buttons off screen. If the content can exceed the available height (long forms, lists, terms, previews), apply the vertical scroll.
* Do not add horizontal scroll to a Modal. Wrap or reflow wide content instead.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.content:

* Warnings
* Success states
* Errors
* Notices
* System status

```text
Warning
Success
Info
Neutral
```

Use semantic types correctly.

rules.title: Page Structure
rules.content:
Use a predictable structure:

```text
Page
 ├── Page Header
 │    ├── Title
 │    ├── Description
 │    └── Primary Action
 │
 ├── Optional Context / Callout
 │
 ├── Filters / Controls
 │
 └── Main Content
```

Do not add every section automatically.

If the page does not need a Callout, Card, Badge, or Divider, do not use it.

Less UI is often better UI.

rules.title: Container
rules.content:
Use `Container` to control readable page width.

Prefer:

```text
Full viewport
 └── Container
      └── Content
```

Do not allow text-heavy interfaces to become excessively wide.

For documentation:

* Keep reading width comfortable.
* Allow code examples to use more horizontal space.
* Keep navigation independent from the reading column.

components.description: The Avatar component displays profile images, user initials, or fallback icons. Supports multiple sizes, variants, online/offline status, rings, and click interactions.

props.name: src
props.description: Image source URL. When missing, or when it fails to load, the fallback initials (or icon) render instead.

props.description: Accessibility label for the image, and the source used to derive initials when fallback isn't provided.

props.name: size
props.description: Avatar dimensions. "responsive" currently resolves to the same fixed size as "md" internally.

props.name: variant
props.description: Shape of the avatar: full circle, rounded corners, or square.

props.description: Shows a status dot using the success color to indicate the user is online.

props.name: isOffline
props.description: Shows a status dot using the muted color to indicate the user is offline.

props.name: ring
props.description: Adds a ring outline around the avatar.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Explicit fallback text (e.g. initials) shown instead of the image; not auto-truncated, unlike the initials derived from alt.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler; when provided, the avatar becomes a focusable, keyboard-activatable button.

props.name: statusPosition
props.description: Corner where the online/offline status dot is placed.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the avatar's root element.

props.name: statusClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the status dot.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the avatar's root element.

props.name: statusStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the status dot.

props.name: imageClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the rendered element.

props.name: fallbackClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the fallback wrapper shown when there is no image.

props.description: Additional classes for the default user icon shown when there is no image and no initials.

props.name: count
props.description: Displays a numeric or custom count badge in the top-right corner; suppresses notificationDot when set.

props.description: Adds an animated ping ring behind the notification dot. Has no effect when count is shown, since the dot itself doesn't render then.

props.description: Additional classes for the badge's root element.

props.name: iconStyle

props.name: textClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the text label.

props.name: textStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the text label.

rules.title: Sidebar Design
rules.content:
The sidebar is navigation, not content.

Keep it visually quiet.

Build it with the Sidebar component (sections with small muted titles, items with icon, label and badge, collapsible icon-rail mode with tooltips, header and footer slots) inside AppShell, which handles the responsive mobile panel. Do not hand-build nav items from Buttons. On mobile-first products use BottomNavigation instead.

This is the content structure for a grouped sidebar, which is only one of several navigation shells. Choose the shell from context (see rule 66: Context-Driven Variety), for example an icon rail for focused tools, a rail plus panel for inbox or chat products, a top navbar for simple analytics, an inset sidebar for modern AI products, or a bottom tab bar for mobile-first apps.

Grouped sidebar content structure:

```text
Logo / Product
Version

Main Navigation

Section Label
Navigation items

Section Label
Navigation items

Resources

About
```

Use:

* Sidebar sections and items for primary navigation links
* Sidebar section titles for labels and grouping
* the item `badge` field for counts, Badge for version information in the header slot
* Icon Button for compact actions
* collapsed Sidebar, which shows labels in a Tooltip automatically
* Divider only when separation improves scanning

Do not:

* Put large cards inside the sidebar
* Use excessive borders
* Use multiple competing accent colors
* Put descriptions beside every navigation item
* Turn every navigation item into a Badge or Chip
* Add decorative illustrations unnecessarily

The sidebar should support the page, not dominate it.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

useFor: Actions on the rows selected in a DataTable

* Products

* Row hover where useful
* Pagination when necessary
* Empty state
* Loading state

Avoid overly dense tables unless the product specifically requires high information density.

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

components.name: Button
components.description: The Button component is a flexible, highly customizable UI primitive built for SaaS applications. Perfect for React authentication UI, form builders, and SaaS dashboard interfaces. Built with Tailwind CSS for modern, responsive design. with TypeScript. It supports multiple variants, sizes, icon positioning, loading states, and full-width layout control - making it suitable for modern design systems and production apps.

props.name: children

props.name: iconAfter
props.description: Icon rendered after the label (hidden while `loading`).

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner + `loadingText` in place of the icons/children and disables the button.

props.name: loadingText
props.description: Text shown next to the spinner while `loading` is true.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to the full width of its container.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style of the button.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls padding, height, font size, and the icon/loader scale.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Styles the inline-flex wrapper around the icon(s)/text/loader.

props.name: loaderClassName
props.description: Styles the spinner shown while `loading`.

props.name: textClassName
props.description: Styles the label text (and the `loadingText`).

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the content wrapper.

props.name: iconStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the icon wrapper.

props.name: loaderStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the loading spinner.

props.name: textStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the label text.

requirements: When an important action exists, give the page one visually dominant primary action.

rules.title: Button
rules.content:
Buttons represent actions.

Hierarchy:

```text
Primary Button
Secondary Button
Tertiary / subtle Button
Destructive Button
```

Every page should generally have one visually dominant primary action, when an important action exists.

Avoid having multiple primary buttons competing with each other.

Example:

```text
Create Project        ← Primary

Import        Export  ← Secondary
```

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

avoid: Putting every field in a separate Card
requirements: Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a placeholder.
The placeholder shows an example or format, stays short and sentence case, and never replaces the visible Label or repeats it word for word.
guidance.composition: Form Section > Label > Input > Description > Error

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Alert / Callout
rules.content:
Use `Callout` for persistent contextual information inside the page.

Use it for:

* Important information
* Warnings
* Success states
* Errors
* Notices
* System status
* Migration messages

Example:

```text
[Warning]

Your storage is almost full.
Consider removing unused files.
```

Use `Callout` when the message belongs to the page's content flow.

Do not use Callout for every notification.

For temporary notifications, use the toast system.

Callout hierarchy:

```text
Error
Warning
Success
Info
Neutral
```

Use semantic types correctly.

rules.title: Cards
rules.content:
Use `Card` when content represents a meaningful visual group.

Good:

```text
Card
 ├── CardHeader (optional)
 ├── CardBody (compulsory whenever there's body content)
 └── CardFooter (optional)
```

`Card` itself renders no padding — it's just the border/background/radius shell. All spacing lives in `CardHeader`/`CardBody`/`CardFooter`. Content placed directly inside `<Card>` without `<CardBody>` renders flush against the border with no padding and visibly breaks the layout, so once you've decided to use Card, wrapping its body content in `<CardBody>` is not optional the way `CardHeader`/`CardFooter` are.

Use Cards for:

* Dashboard statistics
* Settings groups
* Product previews
* Related information
* Independent content blocks

Do NOT wrap everything in Cards.

Avoid:

```text
Page
 └── Card
      └── Card
           └── Card
```

Nested cards should be rare.

If content is already visually grouped by whitespace, a Card may not be necessary.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView
```

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

props.description: Marks the input(s) as required for native form validation.

props.description: Additional classes for each checkbox's `<label>` row.

props.description: Additional classes for the label text.

props.description: Additional classes for the checkbox box/icon.

props.name: checkClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the checkmark SVG inside the checkbox.

props.name: errorClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the error message.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the outer wrapper.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the group container.

props.description: Inline styles for each checkbox's row.

props.name: labelStyle
props.description: Inline styles for each checkbox's row.

props.name: textStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the label text.

props.name: iconStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the checkbox box/icon.

props.name: errorStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the error message.

props.description: Renders a custom checkbox indicator in place of the default box/checkmark.

props.name: iconSize
props.description: Size (in pixels) of the default checkbox icon.

avoid: Putting every field in a separate Card
requirements: Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a placeholder.
The placeholder shows an example or format, stays short and sentence case, and never replaces the visible Label or repeats it word for word.
guidance.composition: Form Section > Label > Input > Description > Error

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

rules.title: Code Blocks
rules.content:
Whenever the UI shows a code block (snippets, install commands, API examples, config files, documentation), use the `react-syntax-highlighter` package (`"react-syntax-highlighter": "^15.6.6"`). Never hand-roll a code block with a plain `<pre>` and manual coloring, and never use another highlighting library.

Install:

```bash
npm install react-syntax-highlighter@^15.6.6
```

Usage:

```jsx
import { Prism as SyntaxHighlighter } from "react-syntax-highlighter";
import { oneDark } from "react-syntax-highlighter/dist/esm/styles/prism";

<SyntaxHighlighter
  language="tsx"
  style={oneDark}
  showLineNumbers={false}
  wrapLongLines={false}
  customStyle={{ margin: 0, borderRadius: "0.75rem", fontSize: "0.875rem" }}
>
  {code}
</SyntaxHighlighter>
```

Rules:

* Use the Prism build and always set the correct `language`.
* The highlighter's syntax theme is the only allowed exception to the theme-tokens-only color rule. Everything around it (wrapper, header, copy button, filename) uses Neuctra UI tokens and components.
* Give multi-line blocks a small header with the filename or language and a copy button.
* Long lines scroll horizontally inside the block (`overflow-x-auto`); the block must never widen the page.
* Inline code in a sentence stays a styled `<code>` element, not the highlighter.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

components.name: Combobox
components.description: A searchable select that combines a text input with a filtered option list. It supports single and multiple selection, async results, grouped options and creating values on the fly, and it shares the label, helper text and size scale of Select and Input so it lines up in any form.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value: a string, or an array in multiple mode.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value in uncontrolled mode.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the next value whenever the selection changes.

props.name: options
props.description: Static option list. Use either this or `loadOptions`.

props.name: loadOptions
props.description: Async option loader, called (debounced) whenever the search query changes while open.

props.name: loadDebounce
props.description: Delay in ms before `loadOptions` is called after typing.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allows more than one selected option.

props.name: creatable
props.description: Shows a "Create ..." row for queries without an exact match.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: Fired when a new value is created; `onChange` also receives it.

props.name: searchable
props.description: Filters options by the typed query.

props.name: groupBy
props.description: Groups options by the string returned from this function. Falls back to `option.group`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder shown in the search input.

props.name: label
props.description: Label rendered above the field.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Helper text rendered below the field.

props.name: error
props.description: Error state. A string is rendered as the message; `true` only toggles error styling.

props.name: success
props.description: Applies success styling to the field.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field as required and shows a `*` next to the label.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and prevents opening the list.

props.name: size
props.description: Field size. Matches Select and Input heights.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Shows a clear button while something is selected.

props.name: name
props.description: Name for hidden form inputs, one per selected value.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Text shown when no option matches.

props.name: loadingMessage
props.description: Text shown while `loadOptions` is pending and nothing is loaded yet.

props.name: maxDropdownHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the option list. Numbers are pixels.

props.name: labelClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the label.

props.name: fieldClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the bordered field that wraps chips and the input.

props.name: inputClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the text input.

props.name: dropdownClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the floating option list.

props.name: optionClassName
props.description: Additional classes for each option row.

props.name: groupLabelClassName
props.description: Additional classes for group headings.

props.name: chipClassName
props.description: Additional classes for each selected-value chip in multiple mode.

props.name: emptyClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the empty and loading messages.

props.name: helperClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the helper/error text.

props.name: fieldStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the bordered field.

props.name: dropdownStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the floating option list.

const teammates = [
  { value: "maya", label: "Maya Chen", description: "Design lead" },
  { value: "omar", label: "Omar Farouk", description: "Frontend engineer" },
  { value: "lena", label: "Lena Fischer", description: "Product manager" },
  { value: "ravi", label: "Ravi Patel", description: "Backend engineer" },
  { value: "sofia", label: "Sofia Alves", description: "QA", disabled: true },
];

<Combobox
  label="Assignee"
  options={teammates}
  placeholder="Search teammates..."
  helperText="The assignee gets notified by email."
/>

When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.description: A searchable, keyboard-driven command menu in a modal overlay. Commands are grouped, filtered by label, description and keywords, navigated with the arrow keys and run with Enter. An optional Cmd or Ctrl hotkey toggles it from anywhere.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state; omit to let the palette manage it internally.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state in uncontrolled mode.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called whenever the open state changes, controlled or not.

props.name: groups
props.description: Grouped commands shown in the list.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the search input.

props.name: searchable
props.description: Enables the search input and label filtering.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Message shown when no command matches.

props.name: recentItems
props.description: Items shown in a "Recent" group when the search is empty.

props.name: recentHeading
props.description: Heading of the recent-items group.

props.name: hotkey
props.description: Letter that toggles the palette together with Cmd (macOS) or Ctrl, e.g. `"k"`. Omit to disable the global shortcut.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the dialog.

props.name: className
props.description: Styles the fixed overlay.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the fixed overlay.

props.name: panelClassName
props.description: Styles the floating panel.

props.name: inputWrapperClassName
props.description: Styles the search input row.

props.name: inputClassName
props.description: Styles the search input.

props.name: listClassName
props.description: Styles the scrollable results list.

props.name: groupHeadingClassName
props.description: Styles every group heading.

props.name: itemClassName
props.description: Applied to every command row.

props.name: emptyClassName
props.description: Styles the empty-state message.

useFor: Cmd/Ctrl+K search across pages and actions in apps with many destinations
avoid: Long forms
Primary page content
requirements: Always expose Cmd/Ctrl+K and keep results keyboard navigable.
Group commands (Navigation, Actions); set `hotkey="k"`; show a visible trigger with a Kbd hint in the header.

rules.title: Modal
rules.content:
Use Modal for focused decisions or short tasks.

Good:

* Confirm deletion
* Create item
* Edit item
* Important settings
* Focused forms

Do not use Modal for:

* Long documentation
* Large dashboards
* Complex workflows
* Information that deserves its own page

If the content requires significant scrolling, consider a page or Drawer instead.

Modal overflow, compulsory:

* A Modal must never grow taller than the viewport. Cap the modal body height (for example `max-h-[70vh]` or `max-h-[calc(100vh-8rem)]`) and give the body `overflow-y-auto`.
* Only the body scrolls. Keep the header (title, close button) and footer (actions) fixed and always visible.
* Never let content be clipped or push the action buttons off screen. If the content can exceed the available height (long forms, lists, terms, previews), apply the vertical scroll.
* Do not add horizontal scroll to a Modal. Wrap or reflow wide content instead.

rules.title: Dropdown
rules.content:
Use Dropdown for actions or compact menus.

Good:

```text
More
 ├── Edit
 ├── Duplicate
 ├── Archive
 └── Delete
```

Do not use Dropdown when users need to compare multiple persistent options.

Use Select instead for form selection.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

components.name: Container
components.description: The Container component is a layout utility designed to control content width, horizontal alignment, and spacing. It provides a simple and consistent way to structure page sections while remaining fully flexible for custom layouts and styling.

props.name: size
props.description: Caps the content width (maps to a Tailwind max-w-* class); "full" spans the parent's full width.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal spacing applied on all sides.

props.name: center
props.description: Centers the container horizontally with auto margins.

props.name: style
props.description: Custom styles (framework independent)

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes merged onto the root div.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the container.

avoid: Adding every section automatically (less UI is often better UI)

rules.title: Container
rules.content:
Use `Container` to control readable page width.

Prefer:

```text
Full viewport
 └── Container
      └── Content
```

Do not allow text-heavy interfaces to become excessively wide.

For documentation:

* Keep reading width comfortable.
* Allow code examples to use more horizontal space.
* Keep navigation independent from the reading column.

```text
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

→ Progress

→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

rules.content:

* Clear labels

* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Code Blocks
rules.content:
Whenever the UI shows a code block (snippets, install commands, API examples, config files, documentation), use the `react-syntax-highlighter` package (`"react-syntax-highlighter": "^15.6.6"`). Never hand-roll a code block with a plain `<pre>` and manual coloring, and never use another highlighting library.

Install:

```bash
npm install react-syntax-highlighter@^15.6.6
```

Usage:

```jsx
import { Prism as SyntaxHighlighter } from "react-syntax-highlighter";
import { oneDark } from "react-syntax-highlighter/dist/esm/styles/prism";

<SyntaxHighlighter
  language="tsx"
  style={oneDark}
  showLineNumbers={false}
  wrapLongLines={false}
  customStyle={{ margin: 0, borderRadius: "0.75rem", fontSize: "0.875rem" }}
>
  {code}
</SyntaxHighlighter>
```

Rules:

* Use the Prism build and always set the correct `language`.
* The highlighter's syntax theme is the only allowed exception to the theme-tokens-only color rule. Everything around it (wrapper, header, copy button, filename) uses Neuctra UI tokens and components.
* Give multi-line blocks a small header with the filename or language and a copy button.
* Long lines scroll horizontally inside the block (`overflow-x-auto`); the block must never widen the page.
* Inline code in a sentence stays a styled `<code>` element, not the highlighter.

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.

* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.content:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```
