rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer is mounted and visible.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called on Escape or overlay click — drive `isOpen` from it.

props.name: children
props.description: Static drawer content, ignored when `renderContent` is provided.

props.name: renderContent
props.description: Render prop for the panel content, given a `close` callback; takes priority over `children`.

props.name: position
props.description: Screen edge the panel slides in from.

props.name: size
props.description: Panel width (left/right) or height (top/bottom); any valid CSS length.

props.name: disableOverlayClose
props.description: Prevents closing on overlay click; also blocks Escape unless `disableEscapeClose` overrides it.

props.name: disableEscapeClose
props.description: Also block Escape. Defaults to `disableOverlayClose`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the dialog when no DrawerHeader is used.

props.name: overlayClassName
props.description: Styles the fixed, full-screen overlay behind the panel.

props.name: overlayStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the overlay.

props.name: panelClassName
props.description: Applied to the sliding panel that hosts the drawer content.

requirements: Keep the underlying page context connected and visible while the drawer is open.

rules.title: Drawer
rules.content:
Use Drawer for contextual content that should remain connected to the current page.

Good:

* Filters
* Detail views
* Editing
* Mobile navigation
* Secondary settings

Drawer is especially useful when the user should keep the underlying page context.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

rules.title: Empty State
rules.content:
Empty states should explain:

1. What is empty?
2. Why it matters?
3. What should the user do next?

Example:

```text
No projects yet

Create your first project to start organizing your work.

[ Create Project ]
```

> No data found.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to protect; any render error is caught by this boundary.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Custom error UI: a node, or a function given the caught error and a callback that clears it.

props.name: onError
props.description: Called with the error and React component stack when an error is caught.

props.name: onReset
props.description: Called after the boundary is reset, by the retry button, `reset()` or `resetKeys`.

props.name: resetKeys
props.description: When any value in this array changes, a caught error is cleared automatically.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the default fallback.

props.name: description
props.description: Body text of the default fallback.

props.name: retryLabel
props.description: Label of the default fallback's retry button.

props.name: showDetails
props.description: Shows the error message under the description in the default fallback (useful in development).

props.name: className
props.description: Styles the wrapper around `children` or the fallback.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the wrapper around `children` or the fallback.

props.name: fallbackClassName
props.description: Styles the default fallback panel.

useFor: Isolating a widget so one crash does not blank the page

avoid: Putting every field in a separate Card

guidance.composition: Form Section > Label > Input > Description > Error

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

components.description: Group related form controls under a semantic fieldset and legend. FormSection adds a title, an optional description and actions slot, a disabled state that locks every control at once, and card or plain surfaces for long settings forms.

props.description: Section title rendered as the fieldset legend.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional supporting text shown beneath the title. Linked to the fieldset with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: actions
props.description: Optional slot rendered at the right of the header, e.g. a "Reset" button.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every interactive control inside the section.

props.name: variant
props.description: `"card"` renders a bordered card surface; `"plain"` renders no surface, for stacking sections inside one card.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding, title size and the gap between controls.

props.name: children
props.description: Form controls and related content.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the fieldset root.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the fieldset root.

props.name: headerClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the legend (header row).

props.name: titleClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the title text.

props.name: descriptionClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the description text.

props.name: actionsClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the actions slot wrapper.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the wrapper around `children`.

components.example:
<FormSection
  title="Project details"
  description="Shown on invoices and in the workspace switcher."
>
  <Input label="Project name" defaultValue="Atlas CRM" />

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.content:

* Focus states
* Screen readers

* Clear labels

* Input descriptions

rules.title: Interaction Design

```text
Default

→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
```

* Navigation

rules.content:

* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:

Recommended:

```text

 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Typography
rules.content:

Recommended hierarchy:

```text
Page title
↓
Section title
↓
Component title
↓
Body text
↓
Metadata
```

Use:

* Strong weight for headings
* Regular weight for descriptions
* `text-secondary` for paragraphs and descriptions
* Muted color for metadata
* Comfortable line-height for reading — but from the text-size class itself (text-sm, text-base, text-lg, ...), not a separate leading-* utility layered on top; the text-size class already pairs a line-height, so adding leading-* alongside it is redundant

See Type Scale (section 52) and Readable Measure (section 53) for exact classes.

Avoid:

* Excessive bold text
* Too many font sizes
* All-caps body text
* Huge headings on every page
* Centering everything
* Adding leading-* on top of a text-size class that already sets line-height

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Paragraph Text Color
rules.content:
Use `text-secondary` for all paragraph text: body copy, section descriptions, card descriptions, and supporting text under headings.

Do not use `text-muted-foreground` for paragraphs. It is too low-contrast for reading text.

Keep `text-muted-foreground` for small, low-priority text only:

* Timestamps
* Metadata
* Captions
* Placeholders
* Helper and hint text
* Disabled states

Use `text-foreground` for headings, titles, and anything that needs full emphasis.

`secondary` is a text color only. Do not use it as a background (`bg-secondary`).

Order of emphasis:

```text
text-foreground        ← headings
↓
text-secondary         ← paragraphs
↓
text-muted-foreground  ← metadata and hints
```

Token values:

* Light theme: `--secondary: #3f3f46`
* Dark theme: `--secondary: #d4d4d8`

rules.title: Type Scale
rules.content:
Use one fixed, responsive type scale on every page:

```text
Display / H1  text-4xl sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl font-bold tracking-tight
H2            text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight
H3            text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold
Body          text-base
Small         text-sm
Meta          text-xs
```

Rules:

* Never use more than 4 text sizes on one screen.
* Add `text-balance` to headings so lines break evenly.
* Add `text-pretty` to paragraphs to avoid single-word last lines.
* Step headings down one level at a time. Do not jump from H1 straight to small text.
* `tracking-tight` only on `text-3xl` and larger. Everything smaller stays at the default tracking.
* Line-height comes from the text-size class. Do not add `leading-*` on top of it.

rules.title: Readable Measure
rules.content:
Long lines are hard to read.

* Paragraphs: `max-w-prose` or `max-w-2xl`.
* Headings may run wider: `max-w-3xl`.
* Never let body text stretch the full width of a wide container.

The layout can be wide. The reading column should not be.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

rules.content:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

components.name: LiveAnnouncer
components.description: An aria-live region that reliably announces dynamic updates, such as cart changes, search result counts and save status, to screen reader users. Hidden by default, or visible as a status line.

props.name: children
props.description: Message (or nodes) announced to assistive technology. Change it to announce something new.

props.name: politeness
props.description: Urgency of the announcement: "polite" waits for the user to be idle, "assertive" interrupts.

props.name: atomic
props.description: Announce the whole region on each update instead of only changed nodes.

props.name: relevant
props.description: Which kinds of changes are announced.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in ms before new content is written into the region (lets screen readers register an empty region first).

props.name: clearAfter
props.description: Clears the region this many ms after announcing, so the same message can be announced again later.

props.name: visible
props.description: Renders the region visibly instead of screen-reader only (e.g. for a visible status line).

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes merged onto the region.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the live region.

requirements: Use semantic HTML first; these utilities enhance it, never replace it.

components.name: LoadingOverlay
components.description: Covers a region, or the whole viewport, with a scrim, spinner and label while its content loads. Children stay mounted so layout and form state are kept, covered controls are taken out of the tab order, and the label is announced to screen readers.

props.name: active
props.description: Shows the scrim while true; `children` stay mounted either way.

props.name: label
props.description: Text announced to assistive tech and shown under the spinner. Pass an empty string to hide it.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional secondary line shown under the label.

props.name: spinner
props.description: Custom spinner node; pass `null` to show only the label.

props.name: spinnerSize
props.description: Size of the built-in spinner.

props.name: blur
props.description: Blurs the covered content.

props.name: fullScreen
props.description: Covers the whole viewport instead of just this region.

props.name: blockInteraction
props.description: Makes covered content unreachable by Tab and pointer while active.

props.name: children
props.description: Region covered by the scrim.

props.name: scrimClassName
props.description: Styles the scrim layer.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Styles the label/spinner stack inside the scrim.

props.name: labelClassName
props.description: Styles the label text.

props.name: descriptionClassName
props.description: Styles the description text.

useFor: Blocking one region while it saves or refetches
avoid: Full-page spinners for normal page loading (use Skeleton)

rules.title: Modal
rules.content:
Use Modal for focused decisions or short tasks.

Good:

* Confirm deletion
* Create item
* Edit item
* Important settings
* Focused forms

Do not use Modal for:

* Long documentation
* Large dashboards
* Complex workflows
* Information that deserves its own page

If the content requires significant scrolling, consider a page or Drawer instead.

Modal overflow, compulsory:

* A Modal must never grow taller than the viewport. Cap the modal body height (for example `max-h-[70vh]` or `max-h-[calc(100vh-8rem)]`) and give the body `overflow-y-auto`.
* Only the body scrolls. Keep the header (title, close button) and footer (actions) fixed and always visible.
* Never let content be clipped or push the action buttons off screen. If the content can exceed the available height (long forms, lists, terms, previews), apply the vertical scroll.
* Do not add horizontal scroll to a Modal. Wrap or reflow wide content instead.

rules.title: Modal
rules.content:
Use Modal for focused decisions or short tasks.

Good:

* Confirm deletion
* Create item
* Edit item
* Important settings
* Focused forms

Do not use Modal for:

* Long documentation
* Large dashboards
* Complex workflows
* Information that deserves its own page

If the content requires significant scrolling, consider a page or Drawer instead.

* A Modal must never grow taller than the viewport. Cap the modal body height (for example `max-h-[70vh]` or `max-h-[calc(100vh-8rem)]`) and give the body `overflow-y-auto`.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: List
rules.content:

* Notifications

* Activities
* Messages
* Search results

Prefer List over Table when users don't need column-based comparison.

rules.title: Alert / Callout
rules.content:
Use `Callout` for persistent contextual information inside the page.

Use it for:

* Important information
* Warnings
* Success states
* Errors
* Notices
* System status
* Migration messages

Example:

```text
[Warning]

Your storage is almost full.
Consider removing unused files.
```

Use `Callout` when the message belongs to the page's content flow.

Do not use Callout for every notification.

For temporary notifications, use the toast system.

Callout hierarchy:

```text
Error
Warning
Success
Info
Neutral
```

Use semantic types correctly.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Popover
rules.content:
Use Popover for contextual controls or additional information without leaving the page.

Good:

* Advanced filters
* Color selection
* Small configuration panels
* Additional metadata
* Contextual actions

Popover content should remain lightweight.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Dashboard Charts
rules.content:
When you build a dashboard (analytics, admin, CRM, reports, any page that shows stats over time or comparisons), visualize the stats with ApexCharts using `apexcharts` + `react-apexcharts`. Do not use another chart library and do not fake charts with divs or static images.

Install:

```bash
npm install apexcharts react-apexcharts
```

Usage (Next.js: load the chart client-side only):

```jsx
"use client";
import dynamic from "next/dynamic";
const Chart = dynamic(() => import("react-apexcharts"), { ssr: false });

const css = (name) =>
  getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name).trim();

const options = {
  chart: { toolbar: { show: false }, fontFamily: "inherit", background: "transparent" },
  colors: [css("--primary"), css("--info"), css("--warning")],
  grid: { borderColor: css("--border"), strokeDashArray: 4 },
  xaxis: { categories, labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  yaxis: { labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  tooltip: { theme: isDark ? "dark" : "light" },
  dataLabels: { enabled: false },
  stroke: { curve: "smooth", width: 2 },
};

<Chart type="area" height={300} options={options} series={series} />
```

Rules:

* Chart colors come from the theme CSS variables (read with getComputedStyle), never hardcoded hex values. Re-read them when the theme switches between light and dark.
* Place each chart inside a Card with a CardHeader (title, short description, optional range selector) and the chart in CardBody.
* Pick the chart by the question: line/area for trends over time, bar for comparing categories, donut/radial only for a few parts of a whole (max 5 slices), sparkline inside stat tiles.
* Keep KPI stat tiles as numbers first; add a chart only where a trend or comparison helps.
* Hide the toolbar, disable data labels on dense series, keep the grid subtle, and set an explicit height so the layout does not jump while loading.
* Charts must be responsive: use `width="100%"` and stack chart cards to a single column on small screens.

props.name: fillClassName
props.description: The filled portion (linear bar or circular arc), alongside `colorClassName`.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?

→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView
```

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages

* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Container
rules.content:
Use `Container` to control readable page width.

Prefer:

```text
Full viewport
 └── Container

```

* Allow code examples to use more horizontal space.
* Keep navigation independent from the reading column.

```text
border

spacing
```

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?

→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView
```

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design

Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Sidebar Design
rules.content:
The sidebar is navigation, not content.

Keep it visually quiet.

Build it with the Sidebar component (sections with small muted titles, items with icon, label and badge, collapsible icon-rail mode with tooltips, header and footer slots) inside AppShell, which handles the responsive mobile panel. Do not hand-build nav items from Buttons. On mobile-first products use BottomNavigation instead.

This is the content structure for a grouped sidebar, which is only one of several navigation shells. Choose the shell from context (see rule 66: Context-Driven Variety), for example an icon rail for focused tools, a rail plus panel for inbox or chat products, a top navbar for simple analytics, an inset sidebar for modern AI products, or a bottom tab bar for mobile-first apps.

Grouped sidebar content structure:

```text
Logo / Product
Version

Main Navigation

Section Label
Navigation items

Section Label
Navigation items

Resources

About
```

Use:

* Sidebar sections and items for primary navigation links
* Sidebar section titles for labels and grouping
* the item `badge` field for counts, Badge for version information in the header slot
* Icon Button for compact actions
* collapsed Sidebar, which shows labels in a Tooltip automatically
* Divider only when separation improves scanning

Do not:

* Put large cards inside the sidebar
* Use excessive borders
* Use multiple competing accent colors
* Put descriptions beside every navigation item
* Turn every navigation item into a Badge or Chip
* Add decorative illustrations unnecessarily

The sidebar should support the page, not dominate it.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)

→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Dashboard Charts
rules.content:
When you build a dashboard (analytics, admin, CRM, reports, any page that shows stats over time or comparisons), visualize the stats with ApexCharts using `apexcharts` + `react-apexcharts`. Do not use another chart library and do not fake charts with divs or static images.

Install:

```bash
npm install apexcharts react-apexcharts
```

Usage (Next.js: load the chart client-side only):

```jsx
"use client";
import dynamic from "next/dynamic";
const Chart = dynamic(() => import("react-apexcharts"), { ssr: false });

const css = (name) =>
  getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name).trim();

const options = {
  chart: { toolbar: { show: false }, fontFamily: "inherit", background: "transparent" },
  colors: [css("--primary"), css("--info"), css("--warning")],
  grid: { borderColor: css("--border"), strokeDashArray: 4 },
  xaxis: { categories, labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  yaxis: { labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  tooltip: { theme: isDark ? "dark" : "light" },
  dataLabels: { enabled: false },
  stroke: { curve: "smooth", width: 2 },
};

<Chart type="area" height={300} options={options} series={series} />
```

Rules:

* Chart colors come from the theme CSS variables (read with getComputedStyle), never hardcoded hex values. Re-read them when the theme switches between light and dark.
* Place each chart inside a Card with a CardHeader (title, short description, optional range selector) and the chart in CardBody.
* Pick the chart by the question: line/area for trends over time, bar for comparing categories, donut/radial only for a few parts of a whole (max 5 slices), sparkline inside stat tiles.
* Keep KPI stat tiles as numbers first; add a chart only where a trend or comparison helps.
* Hide the toolbar, disable data labels on dense series, keep the grid subtle, and set an explicit height so the layout does not jump while loading.
* Charts must be responsive: use `width="100%"` and stack chart cards to a single column on small screens.

```jsx
<Chart type="area" height={300} options={options} series={series} />
```

* Place each chart inside a Card with a CardHeader (title, short description, optional range selector) and the chart in CardBody.

rules.title: Stepper
rules.content:
Use Stepper for multi-step processes.

Example:

```text
Account → Details → Review → Complete
```

Do not use Stepper for ordinary navigation.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author.
