Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

components.name: Table
components.description: The Table component provides a fully responsive and highly customizable data table system. Optimized for dark mode, with inline styles, className overrides, and flexible structure using head, body, rows, and cells.

props.name: children
props.description: THead/TBody sections (and any other content) rendered inside the table. Each direct child is cloned with striped/hoverable/bordered/dense.

props.description: Classes for the outer wrapper div.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the outer wrapper div.

props.name: tableClassName
props.description: Classes for the inner <table> element.

props.name: tableStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the inner <table> element.

props.name: responsive
props.description: Wraps the table in a horizontally scrollable container for narrow screens.

props.name: striped
props.description: Alternates row background colors in the body; forwarded down to TBody/TRow.

props.name: hoverable
props.description: Applies hover background styling to rows; forwarded down to TBody/TRow.

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

components.description: A lightweight sticky table of contents with built-in scroll spy, indentation by heading level and smooth, offset-aware scrolling that also moves keyboard focus.

props.description: Text scale of the entries.

props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark.

props.description: Additional classes for the nav element.

props.description: Inline styles for the nav element.

props.name: titleClassName
props.description: Styles the title.

props.description: Styles the list element.

components.example:
const guideHeadings = [ { id: "toc-demo-install", text: "Installation", level: 2 }, { id: "toc-demo-config", text: "Configuration", level: 2 }, { id: "toc-demo-env", text: "Environment variables", level: 3 }, { id: "toc-demo-deploy", text: "Deploying", level: 2 }, ];

Installation

Run npm install @neuctra/ui and import the stylesheet once in your root layout.

Configuration

Theme tokens live in CSS variables, so light and dark themes switch without a rebuild.

Environment variables

Set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL before building so client components can reach your API.

Deploying

Any platform that runs Next.js works. Static exports are supported too.

useFor: On-this-page navigation for long docs and articles

rules.title: Sidebar Design
rules.content:
The sidebar is navigation, not content.

Keep it visually quiet.

Build it with the Sidebar component (sections with small muted titles, items with icon, label and badge, collapsible icon-rail mode with tooltips, header and footer slots) inside AppShell, which handles the responsive mobile panel. Do not hand-build nav items from Buttons. On mobile-first products use BottomNavigation instead.

This is the content structure for a grouped sidebar, which is only one of several navigation shells. Choose the shell from context (see rule 66: Context-Driven Variety), for example an icon rail for focused tools, a rail plus panel for inbox or chat products, a top navbar for simple analytics, an inset sidebar for modern AI products, or a bottom tab bar for mobile-first apps.

Grouped sidebar content structure:

```text
Logo / Product
Version

Main Navigation

Section Label
Navigation items

Section Label
Navigation items

Resources

About
```

Use:

* Sidebar sections and items for primary navigation links
* Sidebar section titles for labels and grouping
* the item `badge` field for counts, Badge for version information in the header slot
* Icon Button for compact actions
* collapsed Sidebar, which shows labels in a Tooltip automatically
* Divider only when separation improves scanning

Do not:

* Put large cards inside the sidebar
* Use excessive borders
* Use multiple competing accent colors
* Put descriptions beside every navigation item
* Turn every navigation item into a Badge or Chip
* Add decorative illustrations unnecessarily

The sidebar should support the page, not dominate it.


Do not use Breadcrumb on simple pages where there is no useful hierarchy.

The placeholder shows an example or format, stays short and sentence case, and never replaces the visible Label or repeats it word for word.
guidance.composition: Form Section > Label > Input > Description > Error

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.

props.description: CSS text-transform to apply.

props.description: Adds a line-through (strikethrough) decoration.

props.description: Truncates overflowing text to a single line with an ellipsis.

avoid: Excessive bold text or too many font sizes
All-caps body text, huge headings everywhere, centering everything
text-muted-foreground for paragraphs or bg-secondary as a background
requirements: text-foreground for headings, text-secondary for all paragraphs and descriptions, text-muted-foreground only for metadata and hints.
Line-height comes from the text-size class (text-sm, text-base, ...); do not add a separate leading-* utility on top.
guidance.composition: Page title > Section title > Component title > Body text > Metadata

rules.title: Typography
rules.content:
Typography should create hierarchy without requiring excessive decoration.

Recommended hierarchy:

```text
Page title
↓
Section title
↓
Component title
↓
Body text
↓
Metadata
```

Use:

* Strong weight for headings
* Regular weight for descriptions
* `text-secondary` for paragraphs and descriptions
* Muted color for metadata
* Comfortable line-height for reading — but from the text-size class itself (text-sm, text-base, text-lg, ...), not a separate leading-* utility layered on top; the text-size class already pairs a line-height, so adding leading-* alongside it is redundant

See Type Scale (section 52) and Readable Measure (section 53) for exact classes.

Avoid:

* Excessive bold text
* Too many font sizes
* All-caps body text
* Huge headings on every page
* Centering everything
* Adding leading-* on top of a text-size class that already sets line-height

rules.title: Paragraph Text Color
rules.content:
Use `text-secondary` for all paragraph text: body copy, section descriptions, card descriptions, and supporting text under headings.

Do not use `text-muted-foreground` for paragraphs. It is too low-contrast for reading text.

Keep `text-muted-foreground` for small, low-priority text only:

* Timestamps
* Metadata
* Captions
* Placeholders
* Helper and hint text
* Disabled states

Use `text-foreground` for headings, titles, and anything that needs full emphasis.

`secondary` is a text color only. Do not use it as a background (`bg-secondary`).

Order of emphasis:

```text
text-foreground        ← headings
↓
text-secondary         ← paragraphs
↓
text-muted-foreground  ← metadata and hints
```

Token values:

* Light theme: `--secondary: #3f3f46`
* Dark theme: `--secondary: #d4d4d8`

rules.title: Type Scale
rules.content:
Use one fixed, responsive type scale on every page:

```text
Display / H1  text-4xl sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl font-bold tracking-tight
H2            text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight
H3            text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold
Body          text-base
Small         text-sm
Meta          text-xs
```

Rules:

* Never use more than 4 text sizes on one screen.
* Add `text-balance` to headings so lines break evenly.
* Add `text-pretty` to paragraphs to avoid single-word last lines.
* Step headings down one level at a time. Do not jump from H1 straight to small text.
* `tracking-tight` only on `text-3xl` and larger. Everything smaller stays at the default tracking.
* Line-height comes from the text-size class. Do not add `leading-*` on top of it.

rules.title: Readable Measure
rules.content:
Long lines are hard to read.

* Paragraphs: `max-w-prose` or `max-w-2xl`.
* Headings may run wider: `max-w-3xl`.
* Never let body text stretch the full width of a wide container.

The layout can be wide. The reading column should not be.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:

```text

```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.

```text
1024px  small laptop
```

Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

components.name: ThemeProvider
components.description: Light, dark and system theming for your whole app. Persists the choice, follows OS changes, syncs across tabs, and exposes a useTheme hook for toggles and settings screens.

props.name: mode
props.description: Controlled theme mode; omit to let the provider own the mode.

props.name: defaultMode
props.description: Initial mode in uncontrolled mode.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Called whenever the mode should change, in controlled or uncontrolled mode.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: Storage key used to persist the mode.

props.name: storage
props.description: Storage adapter for persistence; defaults to `window.localStorage`.

props.name: applyTo
props.description: Where the theme is applied: the `<html>` element, or only this provider's wrapper (for scoped previews).

props.name: attribute
props.description: How the dark theme is marked on the target: a `dark` class, a `data-theme` attribute, or both.

props.name: disableTransitionOnChange
props.description: Briefly disables CSS transitions while switching so colors change in one frame.

props.name: children
props.description: Content that can call `useTheme()`.

props.name: className
props.description: Styles the wrapper element; defaults to `contents` so layout is unchanged.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the wrapper element.

requirements: ThemeProvider owns the `dark` class; ThemeToggleButton stays presentational.
Wrap the app once at the root; read and change the mode with useTheme.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

components.name: ThemeToggleButton
components.description: A modern, animated dark mode toggle built for SaaS applications. It supports Sun/Moon icon transitions, smooth thumb animation, and works with a context-driven theme system.

props.name: context
props.description:
Theme state and toggle callback. Optional: when omitted, the button reads
the nearest `<ThemeProvider>` from `@neuctra/ui`.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the root toggle button.

props.name: sunClassName
props.description: The sun icon (shown in dark mode).

props.name: moonClassName
props.description: The moon icon (shown in light mode).

props.name: "aria-label"
props.description: Accessible label override; defaults to "Switch to light/dark mode".

components.example:
<ThemeToggleButton
  context={theme}
  className="h-10 w-10"
  sunClassName="text-amber-400"
  moonClassName="text-indigo-400"
/>

requirements: ThemeProvider owns the `dark` class; ThemeToggleButton stays presentational.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: React timeline component for activity feeds, order tracking and changelogs. Done/active/pending statuses, custom icons and timestamps - built with Tailwind CSS.

props.name: items
props.description: Entries to render, top to bottom.

props.name: size
props.description: Density of the list — spacing and dot/icon size.

props.name: itemClassName
props.description: Each `<li>` row.

props.name: connectorClassName
props.description: The vertical connector line between dots.

props.name: dotClassName
props.description: The status dot/icon bubble.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Wrapper around the title/time/description block.

props.name: titleClassName
props.description: Item title.

props.name: timeClassName
props.description: Timestamp/meta text next to the title.

props.name: descriptionClassName
props.description: Item description.

components.example:
<Timeline
  items={[
    { title: "Order placed", time: "09:12", status: "done" },
    { title: "Payment confirmed", time: "09:14", status: "done" },
    { title: "Out for delivery", time: "12:40", status: "active",
      description: "Your package is on its way." },
    { title: "Delivered", status: "pending" },
  ]}
/>

components.name: TimePicker
components.description: A field-style trigger that opens a scrollable, keyboard friendly list of times. Values are plain Date objects, so pairing it with a DatePicker is just two fields writing into the same Date. Steps, bounds, 12-hour display and per-time disabling are built in, and the same TimePicker powers TimeRangePicker and DateTimePicker.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selected time; pass null to represent no selection.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial selected time when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Fired with a Date carrying the picked hour/minute. If `value` (or the
uncontrolled internal value) is already set, only its hours/minutes are
replaced: the rest of the date is preserved, so pairing this with a
DatePicker's value works without extra glue code.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Trigger text shown while no time is selected.

props.name: formatTime
props.description:
Format the displayed time. Defaults to a locale "HH:MM" string, or to
`hour12` when that prop is set.

props.name: hour12
props.description:
Forces a 12-hour (`true`, e.g. "9:30 AM") or 24-hour (`false`, e.g.
"09:30") display when no `formatTime` is given. Leave unset to follow the
user's locale.

props.name: step
props.description: Minutes between each selectable option in the list.

props.name: minHour
props.description: Earliest selectable hour, 0-23.

props.name: maxHour
props.description: Latest selectable hour, 0-23 (inclusive).

props.name: minTime
props.description: Earliest time offered, in 24-hour "HH:mm" form (inclusive). Narrows `minHour` to the minute.

props.name: maxTime
props.description: Latest time offered, in 24-hour "HH:mm" form (inclusive). Narrows `maxHour` to the minute.

props.name: isTimeDisabled
props.description:
Return true to render an option disabled (shown but not selectable),
e.g. to keep an end time after a start time. Receives the option's time
on a fixed reference day; only its hours and minutes are meaningful.

props.name: label
props.description: Label rendered above the trigger.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the trigger when there is no visible `label`.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error state. A string paints the border and replaces helperText below
the trigger; `true` only applies the error styling.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Helper text shown below the trigger when there is no error message.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field as required: shows a `*` next to the label and sets aria-required.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name. When set, a hidden input submits the time as "HH:mm".

props.name: size
props.description: Trigger size. Matches the Select and Input size scale.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the trigger and prevents opening the time list.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Show an inline clear button while a time is selected.

props.name: id
props.description: Id applied to the trigger button.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the trigger button.

props.name: wrapperClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the outermost wrapper.

props.name: labelClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the label.

props.name: iconClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the clock icon in the trigger.

props.name: textClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the displayed time text.

props.name: clearButtonClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the clear button.

props.name: clearIconClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the icon inside the clear button.

props.name: panelClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the popover panel containing the time list.

props.name: optionClassName
props.description: Additional classes for every time option button.

props.name: activeOptionClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the currently selected time option, on top of its active styling.

props.name: helperClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the helper/error text below the trigger.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

avoid: Persistent in-page messages (use Callout)
requirements: Import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — there is no "Toast" component.

rules.title: Alert / Callout
rules.content:
Use `Callout` for persistent contextual information inside the page.

Use it for:

* Important information
* Warnings
* Success states
* Errors
* Notices
* System status
* Migration messages

Example:

```text
[Warning]

Your storage is almost full.
Consider removing unused files.
```

Use `Callout` when the message belongs to the page's content flow.

Do not use Callout for every notification.

For temporary notifications, use the toast system.

Callout hierarchy:

```text
Error
Warning
Success
Info
Neutral
```

Use semantic types correctly.

rules.title: Alert / Callout
rules.content:
Use `Callout` for persistent contextual information inside the page.

Use it for:

* Important information
* Warnings
* Success states
* Errors
* Notices
* System status
* Migration messages

Example:

```text
[Warning]

Your storage is almost full.
Consider removing unused files.
```

Use `Callout` when the message belongs to the page's content flow.

Do not use Callout for every notification.

For temporary notifications, use the toast system.

Callout hierarchy:

```text
Error
Warning
Success
Info
Neutral
```

Use semantic types correctly.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

rules.title: Component Selection Principle

```text

→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".

* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Breakpoint Checklist
rules.content:
Design mobile-first, then check every page at:

```text
360px   small phone
768px   tablet
1024px  small laptop
1280px  desktop
1536px  large desktop
```

At every width:

* No horizontal scroll.
* Touch targets are at least 44px.
* Navigation collapses into a Drawer below `md`.
* Tables sit inside `overflow-x-auto`.
* Images use an `aspect-*` class with `object-cover`, so nothing shifts while loading.
* On mobile, stack content in order of importance (use `order-*` when the source order differs).

rules.title: Alert / Callout
rules.content:
Use `Callout` for persistent contextual information inside the page.

Use it for:

* Important information
* Warnings
* Success states
* Errors
* Notices
* System status
* Migration messages

```text

Your storage is almost full.
Consider removing unused files.
```

Use `Callout` when the message belongs to the page's content flow.

Do not use Callout for every notification.

For temporary notifications, use the toast system.

```text

Warning
Success
Info
Neutral
```

Use semantic types correctly.

```text
spacing
```

components.name: VirtualList
components.description: Render thousands of rows smoothly by mounting only the rows near the viewport. VirtualList supports fixed or per row heights, overscan, measured string heights, infinite loading and empty states, with no dependencies.

props.name: items
props.description: Full data set; only the visible window is rendered.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the scroll viewport. Numbers are pixels; strings (e.g. `"100%"`) are measured at runtime.

props.name: estimateSize
props.description: Row height in pixels, or a function returning it per index.

props.name: overscan
props.description: Extra rows rendered above and below the viewport.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Renders a single visible row; spread `style` onto its root element.

props.name: getKey
props.description: Stable key for each row. Defaults to the item index.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the scroll container.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content shown in place of the rows when `items` is empty.

props.name: onEndReached

props.name: endReachedThreshold
props.description: Distance from the bottom, in pixels, that triggers `onEndReached`.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Draws the bordered card surface around the viewport.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes for the scroll container.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the scroll container.

props.name: innerClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the inner sizing element that holds the rows.

props.name: emptyClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the empty-state wrapper.

avoid: Records that need column-based comparison (use Table)

rules.title: Page Structure
rules.content:
Use a predictable structure:

```text
Page
 ├── Page Header
 │    ├── Title
 │    ├── Description
 │    └── Primary Action
 │
 ├── Optional Context / Callout
 │
 ├── Filters / Controls
 │
 └── Main Content
```

Do not add every section automatically.

If the page does not need a Callout, Card, Badge, or Divider, do not use it.

Less UI is often better UI.

rules.title: Container
rules.content:
Use `Container` to control readable page width.

Prefer:

```text
Full viewport
 └── Container
      └── Content
```

Do not allow text-heavy interfaces to become excessively wide.

For documentation:

* Keep reading width comfortable.
* Allow code examples to use more horizontal space.
* Keep navigation independent from the reading column.

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Sidebar Design
rules.content:
The sidebar is navigation, not content.

Keep it visually quiet.

Build it with the Sidebar component (sections with small muted titles, items with icon, label and badge, collapsible icon-rail mode with tooltips, header and footer slots) inside AppShell, which handles the responsive mobile panel. Do not hand-build nav items from Buttons. On mobile-first products use BottomNavigation instead.

This is the content structure for a grouped sidebar, which is only one of several navigation shells. Choose the shell from context (see rule 66: Context-Driven Variety), for example an icon rail for focused tools, a rail plus panel for inbox or chat products, a top navbar for simple analytics, an inset sidebar for modern AI products, or a bottom tab bar for mobile-first apps.

Grouped sidebar content structure:

```text
Logo / Product
Version

Main Navigation

Section Label
Navigation items

Section Label
Navigation items

Resources

About
```

Use:

* Sidebar sections and items for primary navigation links
* Sidebar section titles for labels and grouping
* the item `badge` field for counts, Badge for version information in the header slot
* Icon Button for compact actions
* collapsed Sidebar, which shows labels in a Tooltip automatically
* Divider only when separation improves scanning

Do not:

* Put large cards inside the sidebar
* Use excessive borders
* Use multiple competing accent colors
* Put descriptions beside every navigation item
* Turn every navigation item into a Badge or Chip
* Add decorative illustrations unnecessarily

The sidebar should support the page, not dominate it.

rules.content:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Cards
rules.content:
Use `Card` when content represents a meaningful visual group.

Good:

```text
Card
 ├── CardHeader (optional)
 ├── CardBody (compulsory whenever there's body content)
 └── CardFooter (optional)
```

`Card` itself renders no padding — it's just the border/background/radius shell. All spacing lives in `CardHeader`/`CardBody`/`CardFooter`. Content placed directly inside `<Card>` without `<CardBody>` renders flush against the border with no padding and visibly breaks the layout, so once you've decided to use Card, wrapping its body content in `<CardBody>` is not optional the way `CardHeader`/`CardFooter` are.

Use Cards for:

* Dashboard statistics
* Settings groups
* Product previews
* Related information
* Independent content blocks

Do NOT wrap everything in Cards.

Avoid:

```text
Page
 └── Card
      └── Card
           └── Card
```

Nested cards should be rare.

If content is already visually grouped by whitespace, a Card may not be necessary.

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Code Blocks
rules.content:
Whenever the UI shows a code block (snippets, install commands, API examples, config files, documentation), use the `react-syntax-highlighter` package (`"react-syntax-highlighter": "^15.6.6"`). Never hand-roll a code block with a plain `<pre>` and manual coloring, and never use another highlighting library.

Install:

```bash
npm install react-syntax-highlighter@^15.6.6
```

Usage:

```jsx
import { Prism as SyntaxHighlighter } from "react-syntax-highlighter";
import { oneDark } from "react-syntax-highlighter/dist/esm/styles/prism";

<SyntaxHighlighter
  language="tsx"
  style={oneDark}
  showLineNumbers={false}
  wrapLongLines={false}
  customStyle={{ margin: 0, borderRadius: "0.75rem", fontSize: "0.875rem" }}
>
  {code}
</SyntaxHighlighter>
```

Rules:

* Use the Prism build and always set the correct `language`.
* The highlighter's syntax theme is the only allowed exception to the theme-tokens-only color rule. Everything around it (wrapper, header, copy button, filename) uses Neuctra UI tokens and components.
* Give multi-line blocks a small header with the filename or language and a copy button.
* Long lines scroll horizontally inside the block (`overflow-x-auto`); the block must never widen the page.
* Inline code in a sentence stays a styled `<code>` element, not the highlighter.

rules.title: Modal
rules.content:
Use Modal for focused decisions or short tasks.

Good:

* Confirm deletion
* Create item
* Edit item
* Important settings
* Focused forms

Do not use Modal for:

* Long documentation
* Large dashboards
* Complex workflows
* Information that deserves its own page

If the content requires significant scrolling, consider a page or Drawer instead.

Modal overflow, compulsory:

* A Modal must never grow taller than the viewport. Cap the modal body height (for example `max-h-[70vh]` or `max-h-[calc(100vh-8rem)]`) and give the body `overflow-y-auto`.
* Only the body scrolls. Keep the header (title, close button) and footer (actions) fixed and always visible.
* Never let content be clipped or push the action buttons off screen. If the content can exceed the available height (long forms, lists, terms, previews), apply the vertical scroll.
* Do not add horizontal scroll to a Modal. Wrap or reflow wide content instead.

rules.content:

```text
 ├── Duplicate
 ├── Archive
```

Use Select instead for form selection.

rules.title: Dashboard Charts
rules.content:
When you build a dashboard (analytics, admin, CRM, reports, any page that shows stats over time or comparisons), visualize the stats with ApexCharts using `apexcharts` + `react-apexcharts`. Do not use another chart library and do not fake charts with divs or static images.

Install:

```bash
npm install apexcharts react-apexcharts
```

Usage (Next.js: load the chart client-side only):

```jsx
"use client";
import dynamic from "next/dynamic";
const Chart = dynamic(() => import("react-apexcharts"), { ssr: false });

const css = (name) =>
  getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name).trim();

const options = {
  chart: { toolbar: { show: false }, fontFamily: "inherit", background: "transparent" },
  colors: [css("--primary"), css("--info"), css("--warning")],
  grid: { borderColor: css("--border"), strokeDashArray: 4 },
  xaxis: { categories, labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  yaxis: { labels: { style: { colors: css("--muted-foreground") } } },
  tooltip: { theme: isDark ? "dark" : "light" },
  dataLabels: { enabled: false },
  stroke: { curve: "smooth", width: 2 },
};

<Chart type="area" height={300} options={options} series={series} />
```

Rules:

* Chart colors come from the theme CSS variables (read with getComputedStyle), never hardcoded hex values. Re-read them when the theme switches between light and dark.
* Place each chart inside a Card with a CardHeader (title, short description, optional range selector) and the chart in CardBody.
* Pick the chart by the question: line/area for trends over time, bar for comparing categories, donut/radial only for a few parts of a whole (max 5 slices), sparkline inside stat tiles.
* Keep KPI stat tiles as numbers first; add a chart only where a trend or comparison helps.
* Hide the toolbar, disable data labels on dense series, keep the grid subtle, and set an explicit height so the layout does not jump while loading.
* Charts must be responsive: use `width="100%"` and stack chart cards to a single column on small screens.

avoid: Adding every section automatically (less UI is often better UI)

Install:

```bash
npm install react-syntax-highlighter@^15.6.6
```

Usage:

```jsx
import { Prism as SyntaxHighlighter } from "react-syntax-highlighter";
import { oneDark } from "react-syntax-highlighter/dist/esm/styles/prism";

<SyntaxHighlighter
  language="tsx"
  style={oneDark}
  showLineNumbers={false}
  wrapLongLines={false}
  customStyle={{ margin: 0, borderRadius: "0.75rem", fontSize: "0.875rem" }}
>
  {code}
</SyntaxHighlighter>
```

Rules:

* Use the Prism build and always set the correct `language`.
* The highlighter's syntax theme is the only allowed exception to the theme-tokens-only color rule. Everything around it (wrapper, header, copy button, filename) uses Neuctra UI tokens and components.
* Give multi-line blocks a small header with the filename or language and a copy button.
* Long lines scroll horizontally inside the block (`overflow-x-auto`); the block must never widen the page.
* Inline code in a sentence stays a styled `<code>` element, not the highlighter.

avoid: Putting every field in a separate Card
requirements: Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a placeholder.
The placeholder shows an example or format, stays short and sentence case, and never replaces the visible Label or repeats it word for word.
guidance.composition: Form Section > Label > Input > Description > Error

rules.title: Input / Form Components
rules.content:
Forms should feel calm and structured.

Recommended:

```text
Form Section
 ├── Label
 ├── Input
 ├── Description
 └── Error
```

Group related fields.

Do not place every field in a separate Card.

Use:

* Input for text
* Textarea for long text
* Select for predefined options
* Checkbox for independent choices
* RadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices
* Switch for immediate on/off settings
* Slider for ranges
* Number Input for numeric values
* Date Picker for dates
* Time Picker for times
* File Upload for files

Placeholders, compulsory:

* Every Input, Textarea, Select, Number Input, Date Picker, Time Picker and search field must have a `placeholder`.
* The placeholder shows an example or format of the expected value: "you@company.com", "Search projects...", "e.g. Q3 marketing plan".
* A placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the Label. Keep the visible Label and add the placeholder.
* Keep placeholders short and in sentence case. Do not repeat the label word for word ("Email" label → "you@company.com", not "Email").

rules.title: Shadows
rules.content:
Never add a shadow yourself, compulsory. Prefer:

```text
background
+
border
+
spacing
```

over a shadow on anything you're styling by hand — buttons, cards, inputs, hand-built panels.

This is about classNames/markup you author. A number of `@neuctra/ui` components ship their own built-in elevation shadow as part of their default design (overlay/floating components like Modal, Dropdown, Popover, Drawer, Tooltip, and others like Table, DatePicker's calendar panel, Avatar's status dot, Kbd, and the Toast notification, among others — this isn't an exhaustive list to memorize). Leave every component's shipped defaults exactly as they ship: never add a shadow yourself, and never strip a component's built-in one with an override either — both are the same mistake in opposite directions.

rules.title: Component Selection Principle
rules.content:
When choosing a component, use this decision process. Always prefer the dedicated @neuctra/ui component over hand-building the same pattern, and call get-neuctra-ui-component for its exact props.

```text
Need an app frame or navigation?
→ AppShell (responsive frame: sidebar + header + main, mobile slide-in panel)
→ Sidebar (grouped, collapsible or icon-rail navigation with badges and tooltips)
→ BottomNavigation (mobile tab bar, 3 to 5 destinations)
→ Menubar (desktop-style File / Edit / View menus)
→ Tabs / Breadcrumb / Pagination / TableOfContents (in-page navigation)
→ CommandPalette (Cmd/Ctrl+K global search and quick actions)

Need a multi-step flow?
→ Wizard (validated steps with Back / Next and async checks)
→ Stepper (progress indicator only)
→ OnboardingTour (spotlight walkthrough of existing UI)

Need an action?
→ Button / IconButton / CopyButton
→ Dropdown (overflow menu) / ContextMenu (right-click menu)
→ BulkActionBar (actions for selected rows) / FloatingToolbar (selection or canvas tools)
→ SwipeActions (touch row actions, always also reachable by keyboard)

Need selection?
→ Select (short fixed list) / Combobox (searchable, async, multi or creatable)
→ RadioGroup / Checkbox / Switch / ToggleGroup
→ Slider / RangeSlider (min and max) / NumberInput / Rating
→ DatePicker / DateRangePicker / DateTimePicker / TimePicker / TimeRangePicker
→ ColorPicker / TagInput / PinInput / FileUpload

Need a form structure?
→ FormSection (titled group of fields) / SettingRow (label + description + control)

Need compact metadata?
→ Badge / Chip / Kbd / Price

Need grouped content?
→ Card (+ CardBody)

Need persistent message?
→ Callout (in the page) / AnnouncementBar (app-wide banner)

Need temporary message?
→ the toast system (import { toast, ToastProvider } from "@neuctra/ui" — not a "Toast" component)
→ NotificationCenter (persistent read / unread history behind a bell)

Need focused interaction?
→ Modal / AlertDialog (confirm destructive or irreversible actions)
→ Drawer / ActionSheet (mobile action list)
→ Popover / HoverCard (preview on hover or focus)
→ Lightbox / ImageGallery (media viewing)

Need clarification?
→ Tooltip

Need structured records?
→ DataTable (sorting, selection, pagination, loading and empty states) / Table (static display)
→ FilterBar (active filters and saved views above a table or list)
→ List / VirtualList (thousands of rows) / TreeView (hierarchies) / Timeline

Need a workspace layout?
→ ResizablePanelGroup + ResizablePanel + ResizableHandle / ScrollArea

Need chat or AI output?
→ MessageList + ChatMessage / AttachmentCard / CodeBlock

Need loading?
→ Skeleton / Spinner / LoadingOverlay (block a region while saving)

Need progress?
→ Progress

Need to display code?
→ react-syntax-highlighter (see Code Blocks rule)

Need to visualize stats or trends (dashboards)?
→ Stat / Sparkline (inline trend) / ActivityHeatmap (activity density)
→ ApexCharts via react-apexcharts for full charts (see Dashboard Charts rule)

Need hierarchy?
→ Accordion / Breadcrumb / Stepper / TreeView

Need resilience or accessibility helpers?
→ ErrorBoundary / SkipLink / VisuallyHidden / LiveAnnouncer / ThemeProvider
```

Never select a component merely because it looks attractive.

rules.title: Accessibility
rules.content:
Accessibility is part of the design.

Always consider:

* Keyboard navigation
* Focus states
* Screen readers
* Color contrast
* Semantic HTML
* Clear labels
* Button names
* Input descriptions
* Error messages
* Touch target sizes

Never communicate meaning using color alone.

rules.title: Interaction Design
rules.content:
Every interactive element should provide feedback.

Examples:

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

Do not animate everything.

Use subtle transitions for:

* Hover
* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

Motion should explain interaction, not distract.

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

avoid: Dividers that do not improve scanning

rules.title: Divider
rules.content:
Use `Divider` only when whitespace is insufficient to communicate separation.

Prefer:

```text
Section

large spacing

Next Section
```

over:

```text
Section
────────────
Next Section
```

Use Dividers primarily for:

* Navigation groups
* Dense settings
* Table-like layouts
* Clearly separated sections

Do not place Dividers everywhere.

```text
No projects yet

Create your first project to start organizing your work.

[ Create Project ]
```

rules.title: Interaction Design

```text
Default
→ Hover
→ Active
→ Focus
→ Disabled
→ Loading
→ Success/Error
```

* Opening/closing
* State changes
* Navigation
* Feedback

rules.title: Do Not Overwrite Built-in Component Design
rules.content:
Use each `@neuctra/ui` component's built-in design — its default spacing, radius, colors, and layout — as-is.

Do not pass a `className` just to restyle a component's built-in appearance because of personal preference. The component's own design is already the intended, consistent look.

Only override with Tailwind's `!` important-modifier (e.g. `!bg-red-500`, `!p-2`, `!rounded-lg`) when there is a real, specific need:

* The component's default would otherwise break the current page's existing layout.
* The default collides or conflicts with the current UI/design of the site.
* The component has no prop for the needed variation, and leaving the default would visually damage the surrounding design.

Never reach for `!important` overrides as a routine styling habit, a stylistic preference, or 'just because'.

Prefer:

> built-in component design → prop-based variation (variant, size, etc.) → `!important` override (rare, only to prevent breakage)

over:

> restyle every component by default with className overrides

A component that has been overridden with `!important` on every use is a sign the component itself, or the way it's being used, is wrong — not that every instance needs forcing.

requirements: Give the user a retry or next action; never show a blank screen.

rules.title: Empty State
rules.content:

1. What is empty?
2. Why it matters?
3. What should the user do next?

Example:

```text
No projects yet

Create your first project to start organizing your work.

[ Create Project ]
```

Do not create empty states that only say:

> No data found.
